study: MA-1163 follow-up independent partition replication of pretrained-weight-selected Mirror addresses
precommit_scope: Separate fresh partition test after development-only direction search; does not retroactively preregister the initial 618201 partition
hypothesis: Teacher-informed sparse coordinate selection of a fixed nonlinear K-Mirror decoder retains trained classifier accuracy with m in [512,768], accounting for index and executable-code bytes. Mirror-specific effect must surpass equal-m sparse plain orthogonal decoder.
data: sklearn load_digits, 1797 samples; per world independent stratified test split 20%, followed by stratified dev split 20% of work data, training rest
baseline: 64->16 tanh ->10 float64, AdamW 900 updates, batch128 lr .008, dev >=.90 gating
mirror: nonlinear 3 K parallel Householder-Givens-permutation mirrored tanh, 3 recurrent residual rounds gamma=.16, fixed transforms and activations, trainable physical coefficient vector m only
compression: target is strictly saved native NN weights, no labels or logits in fitting; choose largest absolute m inverse Mirror coordinates; fit via LBFGS in weight space; report exact sparse indices as stored inference metadata
evaluation: unopened world heldout samples; exact test accuracy/NLL; weight error L2; actual torch.save payload bytes, extra source code bytes, compile/forward wall time

gates.retention: mean per-world Mirror test accuracy is within 2 percentage points of native for m=768 in >=2/3 worlds
gates.mirror_specific: Mirror test accuracy exceeds sparse plain baseline by >=1 percentage point in >=2/3 worlds at equal m and bytes
gates.storage: count coefficient bytes, index bytes, transform metadata, and source code bytes separately; only call compression when final paid bytes < native
gates.uncertain: 3 world partitions of one small digits corpus not natural-task generalization; code source amortization assumptions must be explicit

precision: FP64 CPU single torch thread; high-bit scaling NOT tested
